body:
## Context

Follow-up from the 1.11.0 release-audit OpenCode blocker (containment shipped separately). The calibration spec blesses tracker.depth() as OpenCode's band signal, but the shipped tracker is a monotonic per-session counter that (1) never resets on compaction — markCompacted (lib/build-gate.mjs:34-36) touches a separate Set and leaves depth latched at/above HANDOFF_DEPTH=30 forever — and (2) counts read-only calls (index.mjs:178 records before any read-only filter; test/handoff-deny.test.mjs pumpDepth deliberately pumps with 'read'). A session that compacted back to a small live context is still classified as terminally deep. Fix the signal semantics: epoch/reset depth on compaction, and decide (with the calibration spec, .adlc/specs/context-rot-threshold-calibration.md:451) whether read-only calls belong in the count; amend the pinned tests accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After markCompacted, the depth the handoff gate sees restarts below WARN_DEPTH. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/*.test.mjs` exits 0 with a new compaction-epoch test present.
2. The read-only-counting decision is recorded in the calibration spec's per-adapter table and the code matches it. verify: `grep -q 'OpenCode' .adlc/specs/context-rot-threshold-calibration.md` exits 0 and the cited row states the decided semantics.
title: opencode: depth counter epochs — markCompacted must reset the handoff depth signal, and read-only calls should not count
